candidates.decision_relevance: Reconstruct whether each forecast candidate was formed ex ante and prevent hindsight leakage in evaluating the repeated pullback and range objects.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews repeatedly identify missing candidate definitions, freeze times, evidence cutoffs, horizons, thresholds, and confidence levels; daily outputs contain candidate objects but not their issuance provenance.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Without immutable issuance timestamps, input snapshots, exact specifications, and confidence fields, containment, directional hit rates, calibration, and hindsight leakage cannot be audited.

candidates.decision_relevance: Measure whether the observed bounded ranges provide useful precision rather than nominal containment from excessive width.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews state that range widths, reference prices, benchmark ranges, and matured outcomes are absent; daily range candidates are explicitly based on observed window extrema.
candidates.missing_history_problem: No frozen candidate-to-outcome linkage or naive-range comparator exists, so containment, range width efficiency, false positives, and calibration cannot be assessed.

candidates.decision_relevance: Resolve the recurring mismatch between nominal 1h/4h/12h/24h/72h horizons and shorter or zero-span realized observations.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly report unavailable 1h anchors, zero-span 4h records, and actual spans materially shorter than nominal horizons.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Sparse asynchronous captures prevent clean sequencing of price, aggressive flow, open interest, and relative performance at the stated horizons.

candidates.decision_relevance: Determine whether breadth deterioration or recovery reflects genuine participation changes rather than endpoint selection or changing constituent membership.
candidates.evidence_reference: Reviews repeatedly cite differing breadth endpoints, unknown universes, and changing membership hashes.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Point-in-time breadth cannot establish persistence, constituent-level survival, or comparability across captures when the panel changes.

candidates.decision_relevance: Separate persistent liquidity or positioning stress from transient snapshots when interpreting pullback evidence.
candidates.evidence_reference: Reviews identify missing depth bands, venue coverage, persistence, sampling times, liquidation completeness, and historical option observations.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Single-venue or lower-bound observations cannot establish duration, breadth, or whether microstructure and derivatives stress preceded subsequent price movement.

candidates.decision_relevance: Test whether settled ETF activity provides persistent transmission evidence rather than a single-session contextual observation.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly state that ETF data contain only one settled session without a comparable historical flow sequence.
candidates.missing_history_problem: A single settled total cannot show flow direction, persistence, lead-lag relation, or association with BTC/ETH and breadth outcomes.

candidates.decision_relevance: Provide historical macro cross-checks for episodes where crypto price, breadth, leverage, and relative performance conflict.
candidates.evidence_reference: Multiple outputs state that the FRED macro owner is disabled and that rates, dollar, and volatility observations are absent or stale.
candidates.missing_history_problem: The analyses cannot distinguish crypto-specific transmission or pullback evidence from contemporaneous macro regime effects.

candidates.decision_relevance: Distinguish aggregate stablecoin supply growth from actual deployment or withdrawal associated with risk-asset participation.
candidates.evidence_reference: Outputs repeatedly describe stablecoin levels and aggregate changes but explicitly lack deployment, flow, or dominance history.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Supply growth alone cannot establish whether liquidity reached BTC, ETH, or altcoins, limiting evaluation of transmission and rotation observations.

candidates.decision_relevance: Evaluate the repeated ETH/BTC 0.03 persistence observations as support behavior rather than an isolated level count.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs provide consecutive-close counts but repeatedly note missing near-touch history and longer persistence context.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Consecutive closes above the level do not reveal prior tests, breaches, recovery behavior, or the historical relation between persistence and subsequent relative returns.
